newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse turns strongly bearish.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse turns strongly bearish.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mostly lower on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Tuesday as investors positioned themselves to the sidelines awaiting news from the U.S. FOMC meeting, traders said.
"Everybody was waiting the decision whether the Fed raises rate or not, but that isn't the only reason behind the scale of price falls," said Andrea Keresztesi of ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett.
The BUX index ended at 3,423.72 points, down 89.14.
"This can be explained by Yeltsin's health as well...and for long there haven't been any major news on the market," Keresztesi said.
Traders said the central bank's macroeconomic data, released on Monday, were important guidelines but did not have an immediate impact on share prices.
Spot share turnover totalled 1.21 billion forints, with half of it made by pharmaceuticals firm Richter and chemical firm TVK.
Richter lost 375 forints to end at 7,875, on what traders explained by its status according to which it is regarded as the most sensitive to Russian events.

One of the recent gainers, Inter-Europa Bank continued to rise on what traders explained partly by speculative purchases after news that Banco de Santander of Spain wishes to double its stake to around 10 percent in IEB.
Also, traders said, the bank is regarded a strong financial institution.
IEB closed at 37,400 forints, below the daily peak of 37,600, but 2,350 forints above Monday's close.
